move.detail: { card: string, from: string, to: string, position: number }

columnMove.description: A sortable column was dropped: its id and its 0-based position among the board's columns. The DOM event bubbles to the board and window.

usage.svelte:
<script>
    import { Kanban } from '@sigta-hq/svelte';

    let columns = $state([
        { id: 'todo', label: 'To do', cards: [{ id: 'plumb', title: 'Plumb — one-number widget' }] },
        { id: 'doing', label: 'Doing', cards: [] },
    ]);

    function move({ card, from, to, position }) {
        const source = columns.find((column) => column.id === from).cards;
        const [item] = source.splice(source.findIndex((c) => c.id === card), 1);
        columns.find((column) => column.id === to).cards.splice(position, 0, item);
    }

    function moveColumn({ column, position }) {
        const [item] = columns.splice(columns.findIndex((c) => c.id === column), 1);
        columns.splice(position, 0, item);
    }
</script>

<Kanban onmove={move} oncolumnmove={moveColumn}>
    {#each columns as column (column.id)}
        <Kanban.Column id={column.id} label={column.label} sortable>
            {#each column.cards as card (card.id)}
                <Kanban.Card id={card.id}>{card.title}</Kanban.Card>
            {/each}
        </Kanban.Column>
    {/each}
</Kanban>

shared: Native drag and drop, no library. While dragging, the card moves in the page to where it will land (before the first card whose middle is below the pointer; columns by the pointer passing a column's middle), and the drop reports it.
The board never keeps the order: persist the move and render the new order from your data.
livewire: Listen for sigta-kanban-move / sigta-kanban-column-move on the board (x-on:…) or on window, and persist in your component; its next morph reconciles the board to the order it renders. Without a backend the optimistic move stands.

Only transient drag state lives in Alpine (the runtime's sigtaKanban, so @sigtaScripts is required), never the list order, so morphs stay clean on a keyed, model-bound board: give columns and cards wire:key (a column may sit in a wrapper of your own that carries it).
svelte: onmove / oncolumnmove carry the same detail as the DOM events, which the board dispatches too. Render columns and cards with keyed {#each} blocks from your lists and move the item in the callback: the dropped element is put back first, so your lists re-render from a clean DOM. If the callback leaves your lists as they are, the optimistic move stands.

shared: Use it instead of any hand-written "Saving…" / "Saved" text or loading spans.

livewire: target names actions and/or properties (comma-separated, dot paths match children) on the closest component; it follows their requests by itself, and typing into a watched wire:model shows dirty until it syncs. Validation errors read as failed.

shared: A full rail on desktop; below the tablet breakpoint it becomes a top bar whose burger slides the nav in as a drawer over the page, with a scrim behind it.

The open drawer is a modal dialog: focus is trapped in it, the page behind stops scrolling, and it closes on the scrim, on Escape and on its own close button. None of that applies to the desktop rail. Give the sidebar an aria-label to name both the landmark and the drawer (defaults to "App navigation").

actions sits at the far end of the top row, hard against the burger, and stays visible when the nav is collapsed. Use it for the one or two controls that must be reachable without opening the nav (a search or quick-action trigger); everything else belongs in the nav. Keep it to icon-sized controls: the row is as narrow as the rail on desktop.
Inside a shell with a header, the header carries the brand, actions and burger, so this row is dropped and the sidebar is navigation alone.

A sigta-shell-toggle window event toggles the drawer; the sidebar reports each change as a sigta-shell-nav window event { open }. The shell header's burger talks to it that way, so the two can sit anywhere on the page.

svelte: Works by itself; bind:open when your code opens or closes the drawer. It closes after an Inertia visit (inertia:navigate); in another router, set open = false after navigating.

components.description: The toast region: a fixed stack of paper notes with an inked edge in the variant colour, an optional link or action ("Undo"), dismissed by hand or after a while. Include it once per layout; raise toasts from anywhere.
components.aria: Each toast is role="status" (role="alert" when danger); the dismiss button is labelled.

position.description: Corner of the viewport; bottom ones rise above a visible floating bar.

item.description: One toast (data-variant: success, danger, warning, info).

variant.description: On an item.

leaving.description: On an item that was dismissed and is sliding off.

toast.description: Raise a toast: { text, heading?, variant?, duration? (ms, 0 = stay), link? { text, href, target, rel, download }, action? { text, event, detail } | { text, onClick }, key? (replaces the toast with the same key) }.
toast.blade: sigta-toast (window) — Sigta::toast() from PHP, $sigta.toast() in Alpine, window.Sigta.toast()
toast.svelte: sigta.toast() (import { sigta } from '@sigta-hq/svelte'), window.Sigta.toast(), or the Inertia page prop sigta.toasts

usage.svelte:
<script>
    import { Button, sigta } from '@sigta-hq/svelte';

    async function save() {
        await saveSettings();
        sigta.toast('Your changes have been saved.');
        // or: sigta.toast({ heading: 'Changes saved.', text: 'You can always update this in your settings.', variant: 'success', duration: 5000, link: { text: 'View settings', href: '/settings' } });
    }
</script>

<!-- <Toast /> sits once in the root layout; raise toasts from anywhere on the client -->
<Button onclick={save}>Save</Button>

shared: Variants: success, warning, danger, info.

An action (e.g. Undo after a completion) adds a button that fires its event — or runs onClick from JS — and closes the toast. A key replaces the showing toast with the same key instead of stacking another.
Mount it once per layout, near the end of <body>.
Use a key to replace rather than stack (ticking off five items leaves one toast).
livewire: From Livewire (preferred): Sigta::toast('Saved') or Sigta::toast(heading: 'Changes saved.', text: '…', variant: 'success', duration: 5000, link: ['text' => 'View settings', 'href' => '/settings', 'navigate' => true]) — use Sigta\Ui\Facades\Sigta. A link with 'navigate' => true follows it with wire:navigate.
An action — action: ['text' => 'Undo', 'event' => 'task-reopen', 'detail' => ['id' => $id]] — fires its event through Livewire, so an #[On('task-reopen')] method receives $id.

From Alpine: $sigta.toast('Saved') or $sigta.toast({ heading: '…', variant: 'warning' }); from JS: window.Sigta.toast(…); low level (still supported): $this->dispatch('sigta-toast', heading: 'Saved', variant: 'success').
With wire:navigate, wrap it in @persist('toast') so toasts survive page transitions.
svelte: Raise one from anywhere on the client: import { sigta } from '@sigta-hq/svelte', then sigta.toast('Saved', { variant: 'success' }) or sigta.toast({ heading, text, variant, … }). An action is { text: 'Undo', onClick } (or { text, event, detail } to fire a window event).
From any backend through Inertia: put { sigta: { toasts: [{ text, variant }] } } in the page props and call connectInertia() from @sigta-hq/svelte/inertia once (see sigta-ui.md).

components.name: tooltip
components.title: Tooltip
components.description: Ink bubble on hover/focus with a 150ms open delay; Escape dismisses it. The slot (children) is the trigger.
components.aria: The bubble is role="tooltip"; the trigger wrapper points at it with aria-describedby.

position.description: Side of the trigger; unknown values sit on top.

bubble.description: The ink bubble (role="tooltip"), hidden until shown.

position.description: On the root: which side the bubble sits.

shared: Use it instead of a title= attribute or a custom popover.
A tooltip only adds a hint: an icon-only trigger still needs its own aria-label.
